'''Roko Leni Ukić''' (born December 5, 1984) is a Croatian former professional [[basketball]] player. Standing at {{height|ft=6|in=5}}, he mainly played at the [[point guard]] position, but could also play at the [[shooting guard]] position.

==Professional career==
Ukić was born and raised in [[Split, Croatia|Split]], where he began playing basketball for the youth clubs of KK Split in 1992. He competed on cadet and junior teams for the club, winning the national youth championship twice with the cadet team, and earning the MVP award of the Croatian cadet championship in 2000. Ukić joined the club's senior team in 2000, at age 16. He scored his first professional points on October 14, 2000, as his Split team won the game against [[KK Šibenik|Šibenik]] (93–79). Ukić finished the game with five points.<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://arhiv.slobodnadalmacija.hr/20001016/prilozi-sp1.htm|title = Slobodna Dalmacija archive|date = 2000-10-15|website = arhiv.slobodnadalmacija.hr|language = hr|access-date = 2014-01-17}}</ref>

At age 17, Ukić was already the team's captain. During his five years with the club, he won the Croatian League championship in 2003, and the [[Croatian Basketball Cup|Croatian Cup]] in 2004. In the Croatian Cup final against [[KK Zadar|Zadar]], Ukić scored the winning buzzer beater.<ref>{{Cite web|url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DtM60n_2ggk|title = Ukic buzzer beater|date = 2009-03-26|website = youtube.com|access-date = 2014-01-17}}</ref> Ukić played for Split until 2005, when he was [[2005 NBA draft|drafted]] by the [[Toronto Raptors]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) in the second round, with the 41st pick overall, after averaging 18.5 points and 4.3 assists, in 35.2 minutes per game, for Split in the ABA League.<ref name="draftprofile">[http://www.nba.com/draft2005/profiles/RokoUkic.html Prospect Profile Roko Ukic.]</ref>

Rather than risk being buried on the bench as a reserve player in the NBA, Ukić opted to join [[Saski Baskonia|Tau Cerámica]] of the [[Liga ACB|Spanish ACB League]], a team that had an open spot at the backup [[point guard]] position in 2005. In his first season in a foreign league, Ukić became the first Croatian player to win the Spanish ACB League's Player of the Week award. He got the award after scoring 27 points against [[CB Valladolid]].<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://www.kosarka.hr/main.asp?P=vijest&J=HRV&VijestID=4969|archive-url = https://archive.today/20120903150113/http://www.kosarka.hr/main.asp?P=vijest&J=HRV&VijestID=4969|url-status = dead|archive-date = 2012-09-03|title = Hrvatska reprezentacija ide dalje|date = 2005-11-21|website = kosarka.org|language = hr|access-date = 2014-01-17}}</ref> Ukić won the [[Copa del Rey de Baloncesto 2005–06|Spanish Cup 2006]], and played in the [[2006 ACB Playoffs|Spanish ACB League Playoffs]], where his team eventually lost to [[Baloncesto Málaga|Unicaja Malaga]] in the finals, by a 3–0 series score.

After spending a season with Baskonia, he moved to the Spanish League rivals, [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]], in the summer of 2006, where he also held the backup position at point guard. With Ukić in the line-up, Barcelona won the [[Copa del Rey de Baloncesto 2006–07|2007 Spanish Cup]], but lost the [[2006–07 ACB season|2007 Spanish League Finals]] versus [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]], by a 3–1 series result.

In the summer of 2007, he moved to the [[Lega Basket Serie A|Italian Lega Basket Serie A]] team [[Pallacanestro Virtus Roma|Virtus Roma]], on a [[sports loan|loan deal]], where he was coached by his mentor and [[Croatia men's national basketball team|Croatian national team]] head coach, [[Jasmin Repeša]]. Ukić had his best [[EuroLeague]] season with Virtus, averaging 12.7 points and 2.8 assists per game. He reached the Italian League's national championship finals, and once again his team was only second best. [[Mens Sana Basket|Montepaschi Siena]] won the finals by a 4–1 series result.

On July 16, 2008, Ukić agreed to a three-year deal with the Toronto Raptors.<ref name="raptors">[http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/rokoukic_071608.html Raptors Sign Roko Ukic.]</ref> During his first NBA season, he appeared in 72 games, as a backup at point guard to his former Saski Baskonia teammate, [[José Calderón (basketball)|José Calderón]], wearing jersey #1 for the Raptors. In 12.4 minutes of play, he averaged 4.2 points and 2.1 assists, with career highs of 22 points on February 22, 2009, against the [[San Antonio Spurs]], and 10 assists on March 27, 2009, against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref name="1stseason">[http://www.nba.com/playerfile/roko_ukic/career_stats.html NBA.com Roko Ukic Career Stats Page.] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090308014445/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/roko_ukic/career_stats.html |date=2009-03-08 }}</ref>

On August 18, 2009, Ukić was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], along with [[Carlos Delfino]], in exchange for [[Amir Johnson]] and [[Sonny Weems]].<ref>{{Cite web| title = BUCKS COMPLETE TRADE WITH RAPTORS | url = http://www.nba.com/bucks/news/bucks_raptors_trade_090818.html | work = [[NBA.com]] | date = 2009-08-18 | access-date = 2009-08-18}}</ref> On January 4, 2010, he was waived by the Bucks, at his own request, because he was not satisfied with his role on the team.<ref>{{Cite web| title = Bucks Request Waivers on Ukic | url = http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks_waive_ukic.html | work = [[NBA.com]] | date = 2010-01-04 | access-date = 2010-01-05}}</ref>

After being waived by the Bucks during his second NBA season, in January 2010, Ukić returned to Europe, when he moved to the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi|Turkish League]] team [[Fenerbahçe Men's Basketball|Fenerbahçe Ülker]].<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/64413/180 Euroleague.net Fenerbahce Ulker announces agreement with Ukic.]</ref> He signed a two-year contract on June 17, 2010.<ref>[http://www.fenerbahce.org/fb2008/detay.asp?ContentID=19963 Ukic signed 2 years contract]</ref>

Ukić led his club to the [[2009–10 Turkish Basketball League]] title, by hitting the game-winning shot in Game 3 of the league's finals<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://kosarka.org/main.asp?dir=news&newsid=33513|title = Ukić zabio za pobjedu|date = 2010-05-25|website = kosarka.org|language = hr|access-date = 2014-01-17|url-status = dead|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140102192035/http://kosarka.org/main.asp?dir=news&newsid=33513|archive-date = 2014-01-02}}</ref> and scoring 15 points in Game 6 win by a score of 76–51.<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://kosarka.org/main.asp?dir=news&newsid=33630|title = Ukićevi rasturili Efes, uzeli duplu krunu|date = 2010-06-02|website = kosarka.org|language = hr|access-date = 2014-01-17|url-status = dead|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140102194244/http://kosarka.org/main.asp?dir=news&newsid=33630|archive-date = 2014-01-02}}</ref> The club had also previously won the [[Turkish Cup Basketball|Turkish Cup]], with Ukić scoring 11 points in the Cup's final game versus [[Mersin Büyükşehir Belediyesi S.K.|Mersin BB]].

In the 2010–11 season, Fenerbahçe repeated in winning the Turkish double. Ukić was voted the MVP of the [[2010–11 Turkish Basketball League|Turkish League Playoffs]]. Fenerbahçe also reached the Top 16 phase of the EuroLeague, with Ukić posting averages of 13.2 points, 3.5 assists, and 2.5 rebounds per game. His final season with the Turkish club was injury plagued.

Ukić missed the start of the 2011–12 season, due to a stress fracture in his foot, and later on in the season, he suffered a broken finger.<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://kosarka.org/main.asp?dir=news&newsid=42777|title = Ukić na pauzu zbog slomljenog prsta|date = 2011-12-30|website = kosarka.org|language = hr|access-date = 2014-01-17|url-status = dead|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20141205212321/http://kosarka.org/main.asp?dir=news&newsid=42777|archive-date = 2014-12-05}}</ref>

In 2012, Ukić signed a two-year contract with the [[Greek Basket League|Greek League]] club [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]].<ref name=pbc>[https://web.archive.org/web/20120726155203/http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2012-13-signings/i/98893/7224 PANATHINAIKOS signs playmaker Ukic]</ref> In his first season with the club, he won the third double of his career. In the final of the [[Greek Basketball Cup|Greek Cup]], Panathinaikos beat [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]] 81–78, as Ukić scored 18 points, and won the [[Greek Basketball Cup MVP|Final MVP award]].<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://www.hrsport.net/vijesti/455944/kosarka-grcka/panathinaikosu-slavlje-u-kaoticnom-finalu-grckog-kupa-roko-ukic-mvp|title = Panathinaikosu slavlje u kaotičnom finalu grčkog kupa, Roko Ukić MVP|date = 2013-02-10|website = hrsport.net|language = hr|access-date = 2014-01-17}}</ref>

Panathinaikos and Olympiacos played again in the Greek League finals, and Panathinaikos claimed the title, with a 3–0 series sweep. Ukić was the leading scorer of the finals. In Game 2, he scored 17 points in 23 minutes on the court, helping his team to a 63–52 victory.<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/domestic-leagues/domestic-leagues-2012-2013/greece/i/114249/7590/greek-league-finals-game-2-june-9-2013|title = Greek League finals, Game 2: June 9, 2013|date = 2013-06-09|website = euroleague.net|access-date = 2014-01-17}}</ref>

Ukić played in 28 EuroLeague games in the 2012–13 season, averaging 8.9 points, 2.8 assists, and 2.7 rebounds per game.<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=CJA&seasoncode=E2012|title = Profile on Euroleague.net|date = 2013-06-09|website = euroleague.net|access-date = 2014-01-17}}</ref> He won the [[EuroLeague MVP of the Round|Player of the Round award]] for his performance in Round 8 of the Top 16. Panathinaikos won away at [[BC Žalgiris]], 78–73, with Ukić contributing 21 points, six assists, four rebounds, and a performance index rating of 28.<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/109579/180/top-16-game-8-bwin-tri-mvps-devin-smith-roko-ukic-and-luka-zoric|title = Top 16 Game 8 bwin tri-MVPs: Devin Smith, Roko Ukic and Luka Zoric|date = 2013-02-23|website = euroleague.net|access-date = 2014-01-17}}</ref> After the game, Ukić said he had felt back pain, and had thrown up on the Panathinaikos bench in the final minutes of the game.<ref>{{Cite web|url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LaZI667CHv0&t=1m47s|title = Player of the Game: Roko Ukic, Panathinaikos Athens|date = 2013-02-21|website = youtube.com|access-date = 2014-01-17}}</ref>

Ukić missed the beginning of the 2013–14 season, because of Achilles tendon strains in both feet.<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/117128/180/greens-ukic-expected-to-miss-6-weeks-with-injury|title = Greens' Ukic expected to miss 6 weeks with injury|date = 2013-09-26|website = euroleague.net|access-date = 2014-01-17}}</ref> On August 7, 2014, Ukić returned to Croatia, signing a one-year deal with [[KK Cedevita Junior|Cedevita]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Kapetan reprezentacije Roko Ukić u Cedeviti|url=http://www.kkcedevita.hr/vijesti/tabid/86/id/23749/kapetan-reprezentacije-roko-uki-u-cedeviti.aspx#.U-LYWqNv7Fw|language=hr|access-date=7 August 2014|work=kkcedevita.hr|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140808044207/http://www.kkcedevita.hr/vijesti/tabid/86/id/23749/kapetan-reprezentacije-roko-uki-u-cedeviti.aspx#.U-LYWqNv7Fw|archive-date=8 August 2014}}</ref>

On October 9, 2015, Ukić signed a two-month contract with Italian club [[Pallacanestro Varese]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/178263/pallacanestro-varese-announces-roko-ukic.html Pallacanestro Varese announces Roko Ukic]</ref> Following the expiration of his contract, on December 16, 2015, he parted ways with Varese.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/185038/roko-ukic-pallacanestro-varese-officially-part-ways.html Roko Ukic, Pallacanestro Varese officially part ways]</ref> On January 11, 2016, he signed with [[Pallacanestro Cantù]] for the rest of the season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/187593/pallacanestro-cantu-lands-roko-ukic.html Pallacanestro Cantù lands Roko Ukic]</ref>

On September 1, 2016, Ukić signed with Greek club [[AEK B.C.|AEK Athens]] for the 2016–17 season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/210899/roko-ukic-signs-one-year-deal-with-aek-athens.html Roko Ukic signs one-year deal with AEK Athens]</ref>

On July 22, 2017, Ukić returned to Cedevita, signing a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite news|title=He is back - Roko Leni Ukić signs 2-year deal with Cedevita|url=http://www.aba-liga.com/news.php?id=38501|access-date=23 July 2017|work=aba-liga.com|date=22 July 2017}}</ref> He left club in July 2018. On August 2, 2018, Ukić signed a one-year deal with French [[LNB Pro A|Pro A]] club [[Levallois Metropolitans]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Roko u Parizu; Ukić potpisao za Levallois|url=http://sportklub.hr/Kosarka/Francuska/a64747-Roko-u-Parizu-Ukic-potpisao-za-Levallois.html|access-date=3 August 2018|work=sportklub.hr|date=2 August 2018}}</ref> On July 31, 2019, he had signed with [[Antibes Sharks]] of the [[LNB Pro B|Pro B]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/antibes-sharks-land-roko-leni-ukic/|title=Antibes Sharks land Roko Leni Ukic
|date=July 31, 2019|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=August 14, 2019}}</ref>

On July 16, 2020, Ukić signed with [[KK Cedevita Olimpija|Cedevita Olimpija]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.aba-liga.com/news/43651/roko-leni-ukic-moves-to-cedevita-olimpija/ |title=Roko Leni Ukić moves to Cedevita Olimpija |website=aba-liga.com |date=16 July 2020 |access-date=17 July 2020}}</ref>

On January 5, 2021, he has signed with [[KK Split|Split]] of the Croatian League and the ABA League.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/roko-ukic-officially-inks-with-kk-split/|title=Roko Ukic officially inks with KK Split|date=January 5, 2021|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=January 5, 2021}}</ref> After the end of the 2021–22 season, Ukić was not active for a while. He rejoined Split in December 2022, agreeing to play until the end of the 2022–23 season for free.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://basketball.hr/vijesti/roko-ukic-se-vratio-na-gripe-igrat-ce-besplatno/15047|title=Roko Ukić se vratio na Gripe, igrat će besplatno!|work=basketball.hr|date=3 December 2022|language=hr|access-date=15 December 2022}}</ref>

In February, 2024, Ukić officially announced his retirement from playing basketball professionally.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sportske.jutarnji.hr/sn/kosarka/kosarka-mix/jurica-golemac-vise-nije-trener-cedevite-olimpije-stvari-unutar-momcadi-ne-djeluju-kako-bi-trebale-15315357|title=Roko Ukić se vratio na Gripe, igrat će besplatno!|work=sportske.jutarnji.hr|date=11 February 2024|language=hr|access-date=13 February 2024}}</ref>

==National team career==
Ukić is a former member of the Croatian junior national teams, earning with them a gold medal at the [[2002 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]], and he also played with Croatia's junior national team at the [[2003 FIBA Under-19 World Championship]] held in Greece, averaging 19.8 points, 4.6 rebounds, 4.4 assists, and 2.6 steals per game, as his team reached the tournament's semifinals.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20120322152137/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/32362/sid/3163/tid/2168/tid2//_/2003_World_Championship_for_Junior_Men/index.html Archive.FIBA.com Roko-Leni UKIC 2003 FIBA U-19 World Championship.]</ref>

He has also been a member of the senior [[Croatia men's national basketball team|Croatian men's national team]]. Some of the tournament's he had played in with Croatia's senior national team include: [[EuroBasket 2005]], [[EuroBasket 2007]], [[Basketball at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2008 Summer Olympics]], [[EuroBasket 2009]], [[2010 FIBA World Championship]], and [[EuroBasket 2013]]. Since 2010, Ukić has been the Croatian national team's [[captain (sports)|captain]]. With 1,471 points scored ({{as of|2014|9|lc=on}}), he is third in the list of all-time top scorers for the Croatian national team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.jutarnji.hr/kapetan-zabio-1471-kos-ukic-postao-treci-najbolji-strijelac-hrvatske-svih-vremena--znate-li-tko-su-prva-dvojica-/1217742/|title=Ukić treći najbolji strijelac Hrvatske svih vremena, znate li tko su prva dvojica?|work=[[Jutarnji list]]|date=4 September 2014|language=hr|access-date=4 September 2014}}</ref>

He also represented Croatia at [[EuroBasket 2015]],<ref>{{cite news|title=CROATIA UNVEIL AMBITIOUS EUROBASKET SQUAD|url=http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_W0rFwutQJaUwHCCv5u3xf0.articleMode_on.html|access-date=13 September 2015|work=eurobasket2015.org|date=4 September 2015|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150913045910/http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_W0rFwutQJaUwHCCv5u3xf0.articleMode_on.html|archive-date=13 September 2015}}</ref> where they were eliminated in the eighth finals by the [[Czech Republic national basketball team|Czech Republic]].<ref>{{cite news|title=CZECHS MAKE FIRST QUARTER-FINAL TRIP|url=http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_jqFXDJwUH0AvptWBlLCC63.articleMode_on.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150914214822/http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_jqFXDJwUH0AvptWBlLCC63.articleMode_on.html|url-status=usurped|archive-date=September 14, 2015|access-date=13 September 2015|work=.eurobasket2015.org|date=13 September 2015}}</ref> He also played at the [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2016 Summer Olympics]], and at [[EuroBasket 2017]].

==Personal life==
Roko's father is Zoran Ukić, drummer of [[Daleka obala|Daleka Obala]]. Roko Leni Ukić got his first name after his grandfather, and his middle name after drummer [[Lenny White]].<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://www.24sata.hr/kosarka/zvuci-sjajno-poslusajte-kako-na-bubnjevima-roka-leni-ukic-319714|title = Zvuči sjajno: Poslušajte kako na bubnjevima 'roka' Leni Ukić|date = 2013-06-17|website = 24sata.hr|language = hr|access-date = 2013-09-15}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y7IRGhCCa4w|title = Focus on: Roko Ukic, Panathinaikos Athens|date = 2014-01-14|website = youtube.com|access-date = 2014-01-17}}</ref>

Roko also plays the drums. In the summer of 2023, Roko's band Stereotrip, released their first album titled "Mimo svijeta".<ref>{{Cite web|url = https://www.tportal.hr/showtime/clanak/kosarkas-roko-leni-ukic-u-bogatoj-karijeri-nastupao-je-za-velike-europske-klubove-igrao-u-nba-ligi-a-sada-okrece-novu-zivotnu-stranicu-foto-20220703|title = Košarkaš Roko Leni Ukić u bogatoj karijeri nastupao je za velike europske klubove, igrao u NBA ligi, a sada okreće novu životnu stranicu|date = 6 July 2022|website = tportal.hr |language = hr|accessdate = 6 October 2022}}</ref> In 2025 he and his band released their second album titled "Divlje zvijeri" under the Croatia Records label.<ref>{{Cite web|url = https://www.tportal.hr/sport/clanak/rock-bend-legendarnog-kapetana-hrvatske-je-izbacio-drugi-album-pogledajte-kako-izgledaju-i-kako-zvuce-20250515|title=Rock bend legendarnog kapetana Hrvatske je izbacio drugi album; pogledajte kako izgledaju i kako zvuče|date = 15 May 2025|website = tportal.hr |language = hr| accessdate = 22 May 2025}}</ref>

Ukić is married to his wife Tamara (b. 1985), and he has a daughter, Sara, born October 20, 2007, in [[Rome]].<ref name="sara">[http://www.virtusroma.it/internal.asp?cat_id=11&art_id=1126 Sara Ukic has been born.] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110929014044/http://www.virtusroma.it/internal.asp?cat_id=11&art_id=1126 |date=September 29, 2011 }}</ref> He also has a son, Luka.
